- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast slope to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast momentum by 10–15% in next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80) and forecast is still rising, adjust downward by 2–4 points.  
- Forecast horizon 30d often underestimates downside risk — add 1–2% buffer for negative sentiment or volatility spikes.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.8 → -0.2 → +0.6), model should anticipate volatility and widen forecast range.  
- When true outcome deviates >5% from forecast, check sentiment history for recent “sudden shift” — if yes, adjust forecast direction by 1–2 steps backward.
